name: Session Cookie Flags Explicitly Disabled (Secure/HttpOnly)
attack_scenario: Without HttpOnly, any reflected/stored XSS reads document.cookie and exfiltrates the session id; without Secure, the cookie rides over a plain-HTTP request (SSL-strip or a mixed-content asset) and is sniffed on the wire, letting the attacker hijack the session.
negative_test_hint: after login, attempt to read the session id via "document.cookie" and assert the cookie is unreadable and its Set-Cookie carries HttpOnly and Secure

exemplar.explanation: IPA 'Anzen na Web Site no Tsukurikata' (Secure/HttpOnly guidance) and the KISA Java secure-coding guide both require session cookies to carry Secure (HTTPS-only) and HttpOnly (no JS access). Calling setSecure(false)/setHttpOnly(false) on a servlet Cookie strips those protections explicitly; setting both to true keeps the session id off unencrypted channels and away from scripts.
